metadata.course: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems
metadata.attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
metadata.scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
metadata.description: An introductory biology course: the chemistry of life, cell structure and transport, bioenergetics, genetics and inheritance, evolution, and ecology.

concepts.title: Active transport
concepts.summary: Moving a substance against its gradient costs energy, which is why it stops when respiration stops.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Aerobic respiration
concepts.summary: Aerobic respiration oxidises glucose completely, releasing far more energy per molecule than the anaerobic route.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Alleles, genotype and phenotype
concepts.summary: Genotype is the allele combination and phenotype is the observable result of it plus the environment.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Anaerobic respiration
concepts.summary: Without oxygen, glucose is only partly broken down, which is why muscles fatigue and yeast ferments.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Antibiotic resistance as observed evolution
concepts.summary: Resistance spreads because the survivors reproduce, which is selection visible on a human timescale.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: ATP as the energy currency
concepts.summary: ATP couples energy-releasing reactions to energy-requiring ones so the cell does not rely on heat.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Biodiversity and conservation
concepts.summary: Diverse ecosystems are more resilient, so conservation is about protecting interactions not just species.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Biotic and abiotic factors
concepts.summary: Living and non-living factors interact, and a change in one usually propagates through the other.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Blood glucose regulation
concepts.summary: Insulin and glucagon act in opposition to keep blood glucose within a narrow range.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Blood, vessels and their adaptation
concepts.summary: Arteries, veins and capillaries differ in wall structure according to the pressure and exchange each must handle.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Carbohydrates
concepts.summary: Simple sugars join into polysaccharides that serve as immediate fuel or stored energy.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Carbon and nitrogen cycles
concepts.summary: Matter cycles while energy flows, which is why nutrients can be reused but energy cannot.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Cell cycle and mitosis
concepts.summary: Mitosis produces genetically identical cells for growth and repair, with checkpoints that catch damage.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Cell membrane structure
concepts.summary: The fluid mosaic model explains selective permeability as proteins embedded in a moving lipid bilayer.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Cell specialisation and differentiation
concepts.summary: All cells in an organism share the same DNA, and differentiation is about which genes are expressed.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Classification and phylogeny
concepts.summary: Modern classification aims to reflect evolutionary relatedness rather than superficial similarity.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Diffusion and factors affecting it
concepts.summary: Net movement down a concentration gradient depends on gradient size, distance, temperature and surface area.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: DNA structure and replication
concepts.summary: Complementary base pairing lets a double helix copy itself accurately and explains mutation.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Dominant, recessive and codominant alleles
concepts.summary: Codominance produces both phenotypes at once, which is why AB blood type is not a blend.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Energy transfer and pyramids
concepts.summary: A pyramid of biomass or energy quantifies the loss between trophic levels.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Enzyme inhibition
concepts.summary: Competitive and non-competitive inhibitors both slow a reaction but differ in whether more substrate helps.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Enzymes as biological catalysts
concepts.summary: Enzymes are proteins that lower activation energy and are unchanged by the reaction they speed up.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells
concepts.summary: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles, which is the deepest structural divide among cells.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Evidence for evolution
concepts.summary: Fossils, comparative anatomy, embryology and molecular sequences are independent lines that agree.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Exchange surfaces in multicellular organisms
concepts.summary: Villi, alveoli and gills all increase surface area and maintain a gradient, the same two requirements every time.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Extinction and biodiversity loss
concepts.summary: A species becomes extinct when it cannot adapt fast enough to a change in its environment.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Factors affecting enzyme activity
concepts.summary: Temperature and pH change activity by changing shape, and beyond the optimum the enzyme denatures.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Food chains, webs and trophic levels
concepts.summary: Energy passes up a chain and most of it is lost at each step, which is why chains are short.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Food tests and biological molecules in practice
concepts.summary: Benedict's, iodine, Biuret and emulsion tests identify each class of molecule by a characteristic colour change.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Genes and the genetic code
concepts.summary: A triplet of bases codes for one amino acid, so the code is degenerate but unambiguous.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Genetic disorders and screening
concepts.summary: Many disorders follow simple Mendelian patterns, which makes carrier testing possible.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Homeostasis and negative feedback
concepts.summary: A receptor, a coordinator and an effector adjust conditions back toward a set point.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Hormones and the endocrine system
concepts.summary: Hormones travel in blood and act on target cells that carry the matching receptor.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Human impact on ecosystems
concepts.summary: Pollution, habitat loss and introduced species each disrupt an ecosystem through a different mechanism.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Investigating photosynthesis
concepts.summary: Counting oxygen bubbles or measuring biomass gain turns an invisible process into a measurable rate.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Investigating respiration rate
concepts.summary: Respiration rate is measured indirectly through a proxy such as oxygen uptake or heat release.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Leaf structure and gas exchange
concepts.summary: Stomata, air spaces and a large flat surface all exist to make gas exchange efficient while limiting water loss.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Levels of ecological organisation
concepts.summary: Organism, population, community and ecosystem are nested levels with different questions at each.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Limiting factors
concepts.summary: At any moment the rate is limited by whichever factor is in shortest supply.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Lipids
concepts.summary: Triglycerides store energy densely and phospholipids form the membranes that compartmentalise cells.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Lock and key and induced fit
concepts.summary: A substrate fits an enzyme's active site, and the site adjusts slightly to grip it.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Meiosis and gamete formation
concepts.summary: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and reshuffles genes, which is what creates genetic variation.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Microscopy and magnification
concepts.summary: Magnification and resolution are different limits, and resolution is what actually restricts detail.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Monohybrid crosses and Punnett squares
concepts.summary: A Punnett square enumerates the possible offspring from the gametes each parent can produce.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Mutations and their consequences
concepts.summary: A change in the base sequence may change the protein's shape, and whether it matters depends on where it lands.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Natural selection
concepts.summary: Heritable variation plus differential survival changes the frequency of traits across generations.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Nervous coordination and reflexes
concepts.summary: A reflex arc bypasses conscious processing, which is why a reflex is faster than a decision.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Nucleic acids
concepts.summary: DNA stores information in a stable double strand while RNA carries and interprets it.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Organelles and their functions
concepts.summary: Each organelle specialises in one job, and the cell's capability follows from which organelles it has.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Osmosis and water potential
concepts.summary: Water moves across a partially permeable membrane toward lower water potential, which is why cells shrink or burst.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Pedigree analysis
concepts.summary: A family tree lets the inheritance pattern be inferred from who is and is not affected.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Photosynthesis and its requirements
concepts.summary: Light energy converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen, storing energy in chemical bonds.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Population dynamics
concepts.summary: Populations grow until a limiting factor caps them, and predator-prey numbers oscillate out of phase.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Protein synthesis
concepts.summary: Transcription copies DNA into mRNA and translation reads it at the ribosome to build a protein.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Proteins and their structure levels
concepts.summary: A protein's function follows from its folded shape, which follows from its amino acid sequence.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Sex determination and sex linkage
concepts.summary: Genes carried on a sex chromosome are inherited differently because the two sexes have different chromosome sets.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Speciation and isolation
concepts.summary: Reproductive isolation lets two populations diverge until they can no longer interbreed.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Stem cells
concepts.summary: Stem cells can divide and become other cell types, which is why they are both promising and contested.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Surface area to volume ratio
concepts.summary: As a cell grows its surface area to volume ratio falls, which limits how large a cell can be.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: The circulatory system
concepts.summary: A double circulation keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate, which supports warm-blooded metabolism.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: The respiratory system
concepts.summary: Alveoli maximise surface area and keep a gradient, the same two requirements as every exchange surface.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Thermoregulation
concepts.summary: The body balances heat gain and loss through vasodilation, sweating, shivering and vasoconstriction.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Variation and its sources
concepts.summary: Genetic variation comes from mutation and meiosis, while environmental variation comes from conditions.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems

concepts.title: Water and its biological properties
concepts.summary: Hydrogen bonding gives water its high specific heat and solvent power, which is why life depends on it.

provenance.source: Biology — Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecosystems
